title: Native total-limit projection identity for compact support
statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-qcqs-compact-support-strict-reduction-comparison, for any coefficient derived-system calculi SX and SY there exists a natural isomorphism gamma from the recorded integral compact-support functor into the native strict-system total limit, and gamma followed by each native total-limit projection and finite evaluation equals the finite scalar-adjunction unit followed by the recorded finite compact-support reduction isomorphism.

source.note: The construction and projection equation are the third proof step of the parent node.

proof.text: Project the fixed integral action realization from representative independence. Its chosen right-derived total-limit functor has a universal unit and normalized projections. The generic uniqueness theorem for right-derived functors compares it to coefficientConstantTowerLimit; its unit equation identifies every normalized projection. Whiskering this comparison gives the recorded integral action comparison to the standard total limit, with its chosen Roos projections. This is proved directly by the private recordedTowerLimit helper.

Compare the chosen whole strict tower to the native compact-support system after completed-scalar restriction. Whisker this isomorphism by the constructible inclusion and the standard total limit, and compose with the preceding comparison to construct gamma.

Naturality of the standard total-limit projection moves the map of the strict-tower comparison past the projection. The finite normalization of that comparison leaves the recorded tower evaluation, so the existing Roos equation applies. Transport its heterogeneous source through sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor_obj. Expand sfCompactSupportFiniteReductionIso as reduction of that object transport followed by the specified projection adjunct; naturality of the finite scalar-adjunction unit and the inverse laws of its Hom equivalence give the required equation.

proof_origin.place: Strict quotient compatibility and total inverse limit, assembling representative independence and generic right-derived uniqueness directly, with explicit scalar-adjunction transport

theorem qcqsCompactSupport_strictReductionGamma
    (SX : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (SY : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y) :
    let N := SX.reduction ⋙ ProEtale.VaryingRing.J (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
        (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) c.i ⋙
      ProEtale.VaryingRing.P (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
        (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) c.g
    let e (n : ℕ) : N ⋙ coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E Y n ≅
        scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n ⋙
          sfAmbientCompactSupportCandidate (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) c :=
      Functor.isoWhiskerLeft SX.reduction (compactSupportSystemEvaluation l E c n) ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerRight (SX.reductionEvaluation n)
          (sfIntrinsicCompactSupport c (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
    ∃ (γ : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l K₀ hl c E ⋙
          (sfIntegralConstructible l E Y).ι ≅
        (sfIntegralConstructible l E X).ι ⋙ N ⋙
          coefficientSequenceLimit l E Y),
      ∀ (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) (n : ℕ),
        γ.hom.app K ≫ (coefficientSequenceProjection l E Y n).app
              ((N).obj K.obj) ≫
            (coefficientFiniteDerivedRestriction l E Y n).map
              ((e n).hom.app K.obj) =
          (coefficientFiniteAdjunction l E Y n).unit.app
              ((sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l K₀ hl c E).obj K).obj ≫
            (coefficientFiniteDerivedRestriction l E Y n).map
              (sfCompactSupportFiniteReductionIso l K₀ hl c E K n).hom
